transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I’m exhausted all the time, like I’m running on empty no matter how much I rest. I just don’t have the energy to keep up with anything anymore, and it's gotten to the point where I just can't keep going like this.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or has the lack of energy been your main concern?

They really go hand-in-hand for me, and both have been crushing. Along with having zero energy, I feel this heavy, empty hopelessness most days, like my whole life has just been a waste. I'm just completely drained, both in my body and my spirit.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of exhaustion and hopelessness, was it a gradual onset or did it start suddenly?

It’s been building up gradually for well over a year now, starting shortly after they announced the restructuring at my job. As I began trying to plan for retirement, this heavy exhaustion and hopelessness just steadily took over, and I've been stuck in it ever since.
Have you had any periods in the past year where you felt significantly better for a couple of months or more, or has this low energy and hopelessness been constant since it started?

This low energy and hopeless feeling has pretty much been my constant baseline for over a year now. There was a brief stretch earlier this year where the depression didn't feel quite as crushing and I could enjoy seeing my grandson a little bit, but that heavy, drained feeling never truly went away.
Can you tell me more about that brief stretch earlier this year when you felt a little better, was that a full return to your normal self or just a slight improvement in your mood and energy?

It wasn’t a full return to my normal self at all, just a slight lift where I didn't feel quite as crushed and could enjoy seeing my grandson a little bit. Even though my mood was slightly better then, the voice whispering my name at night and the belief that management was tracking me still kept going just the same.
Can you tell me more about the voice whispering your name at night, how often does this happen and when did it start?

It happens pretty often, especially at night when I'm alone, and I hear this low male voice muttering my name and calling me a failure like someone is standing right behind me. It started several months after my mood first went downhill, and it's been going on steadily for most of this past year.
Have you ever seen anything that others cannot see, or believed things that you later found out were not true, in addition to hearing the voice whispering your name?

No, I haven't seen anything unusual that isn't really there. But I am absolutely convinced that the management at my job is quietly tracking everything I do and say, even when I'm at home. They're doing it to make sure I get pushed out of my job and to guarantee that nobody else will ever hire me again.
Can you think of any reason why the management at your job would be tracking you, or is this belief based on something specific that has happened to you?

It started when they announced the restructuring to phase out senior staff, and I'm convinced they're monitoring me even at home to find a reason to push me out. They want to make sure I'm completely discredited so that nobody else will ever hire me again once I'm gone. It's like they need to be absolutely sure I'm out of the picture for good.
Have you ever taken any actions to try to protect yourself from being tracked by your job's management, such as changing your daily routines or taking steps to secure your home?

I'm still convinced they're tracking me, but I haven't actually done anything to secure my home or change my routine. I'm just too exhausted to even try, and honestly, I wouldn't even know what I could do to stop them anyway.
Do you think the belief that your job's management is tracking you is something that might be exaggerated or not entirely true, or do you believe it's a fact, no matter what others might say?

It’s not an exaggeration at all, and I believe it is absolutely true. I am completely convinced they are tracking me even when I'm at home to make sure I'm pushed out. It is a fact to me, regardless of what anyone else might say.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that you held to be true, but later found out were not based in reality, aside from the belief about your job's management tracking you?
No, I've never had any other beliefs like that. The only thing of that nature is my absolute conviction that the management at my job is tracking me.
Do you think the voice whispering your name and the belief that you're being tracked by your job's management are connected, or are they separate things that are happening to you?

They definitely feel closely connected to me. Both the voice calling me a failure and the tracking started around the same time, right when I began sinking into that deep depression about the work restructuring. They just feel like part of the same overwhelming weight, constantly telling me that I've failed and that I'm being pushed out.

Do you think that if you were to retire or leave your job, the voice would stop whispering your name and the management would stop tracking you, or do you believe these things would continue regardless of your employment status?

I'm convinced they would keep tracking me even after I retire, because their goal is to make sure I'm blacklisted so no one else will ever hire me. And that voice calling me a failure feels so real and deeply personal that I don't think it would just stop when I stop working. I feel like I'll never really escape any of it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that the voice whispering your name and the belief about being tracked might be a product of your own mind, rather than an actual external reality?

I’ve wondered at times if I'm just losing my mind from all this stress, but it all feels far too real to dismiss. The voice sounds exactly like someone is standing right behind me in the room, and I remain deeply convinced that management is tracking me. It makes it incredibly difficult to believe it's just my mind playing tricks on me.
Can you describe a specific situation where you felt like the management was tracking you, and how you knew it was happening?

It’s hard to point to a physical bug or a camera, but I can just feel this constant, heavy presence, like they are listening to my private conversations at home to find any excuse to push me out. I just know in my gut that they are tracking my every move so they can discredit me and make sure I never get hired anywhere else.
Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things or feeling things on your skin, in addition to hearing the voice whispering your name?
No, I haven't seen anything unusual or felt anything strange on my skin. It is strictly that low male voice whispering my name and calling me a failure, especially when I'm alone at night.
Do you think that the voice and the feeling of being tracked would still be present if your depressive symptoms, such as the feelings of hopelessness and exhaustion, were to significantly improve?

Yes, I believe they would still be present, because they actually did continue even when my depression lifted a bit earlier this year. During that brief stretch when my mood was slightly better and I could enjoy seeing my grandson, the voice at night and the feeling of management tracking me didn't stop at all.
Can you tell me if there are any times when the voice whispering your name or the belief that you're being tracked by management seems to get worse or better, and what might trigger those changes?

The voice whispering my name is definitely much worse at night after work, especially when the TV is off and I'm completely alone in the house. As for the tracking, it stays pretty constant, and even during that brief time earlier this year when my mood lifted a bit, both the voice and the belief that they were watching me didn't get any better.
Do you think the voice whispering your name and the belief about being tracked are related to your feelings of hopelessness and exhaustion, or do they seem like separate issues to you?

They feel very connected because the voice and the tracking really took hold and weighed on me at the exact same time I sank into this heavy, hopeless mood. But they also seem somewhat separate, because during that brief stretch earlier this year when my mood wasn't quite as crushing, the voice and the feeling of being tracked still kept happening anyway.
Can you describe in more detail why you believe the management at your job is specifically targeting you, and what evidence you think supports this belief?

Since the restructuring started, I've been convinced they are quietly tracking everything I do and say, even at home, to make sure I'm pushed out. They want to discredit me completely so that absolutely nobody else will hire me once I'm gone from this job. It's the only way they can guarantee I'm permanently out of the picture.

Do you think the voice whispering your name and the belief about management tracking you would change or stop if you were to receive evidence or assurance that you are not being tracked, or do you believe these things would continue regardless of any external proof?

It is hard to imagine any proof changing my mind because the tracking feels so incredibly real and the voice is so vivid. Even if someone tried to assure me otherwise, I feel deeply convinced that management is watching me and that the voice would still be there. It just feels like an undeniable reality to me.

Have you ever experienced any other types of delusions, such as feeling like you have special powers or that you're in danger, in addition to the belief that you're being tracked by your job's management?

I definitely feel in danger of having my life and future completely ruined by the management tracking me, because they want to make sure I'm never hired again. However, I don't have any special powers or other unusual beliefs like that. It is just this tracking that I am convinced is happening.

Can you think of any situation or event that could happen in the future where you might consider the possibility that the voice and the tracking could be a part of your illness rather than an actual external reality?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about it that way. Because the voice and the tracking feel so incredibly real to me right now, it's just hard to imagine any situation that would make me doubt them.

Do you think the voice whispering your name and the feeling of being tracked would still be present if you were in a completely different environment, away from your job and home, for an extended period of time?

I'm really not sure, and I haven't thought about it much because it's hard to imagine being anywhere else right now. The voice and the tracking feel so real and tied to my life here that I feel like they would follow me wherever I went.
Have you ever had any periods where the voice stopped whispering your name for a significant amount of time, or has it been consistently present since it started?

No, it hasn't really stopped at all since it first started about a year ago. It has been bothering me pretty steadily, and even during that brief stretch earlier this year when my mood lifted slightly and I enjoyed seeing my grandson, the voice was still whispering to me at night.
Can you tell me if the voice whispering your name ever comments on your actions or thoughts, or does it mainly just call you a failure?

No, it doesn't really comment on what I'm doing or thinking. It mostly just mutters my name and calls me a failure over and over. It sounds so incredibly real, especially when I'm sitting alone at night, and it really shakes me up when I'm already so tired.
Can you describe how the voice whispering your name and the belief about management tracking you relate to each other, and do you think one causes the other or if they are separate entities?

I'm really not sure how the voice and the tracking relate, or if one of them is causing the other. They both just feel like different parts of the same heavy, overwhelming experience I've been going through lately. It's just hard to make sense of how they connect when everything in my life feels so exhausting.

Do you think the voice whispering your name and the belief about being tracked would still be present if you were treated for your depressive symptoms and they significantly improved, or do you believe these are separate issues that would require separate treatment?

I feel like they might be separate issues, because during that stretch earlier this year when my mood wasn't quite as heavy and I could enjoy seeing my grandson, the voice still whispered my name and I still felt management was tracking me. Because of that, I worry they wouldn't just go away even if my depression got better. It feels like they might need their own treatment to make them stop.
Have you ever experienced any episodes where the voice whispering your name seemed to respond to your thoughts or actions, or has it always been a one-way experience?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about it that way. The voice usually just mutters my name and calls me a failure, and I don't ever interact with it. It has always just been a one-way experience for me.
Do you think the voice whispering your name and the feeling of being tracked are under your control, or do they happen completely outside of your control?

They are completely outside of my control. The voice sounds as real as an actual person standing right behind me, and since the tracking is being done by management, I have absolutely no power to stop or control either of them.
